source: Vynatheya, Mardling and Hamers 2023, MNRAS 525, 3 (arXiv 2301.09930); weights from https://github.com/pavanvyn/quadruple-stability, mlp_model_2p2_ghost_v1.2.2.pkl (read 2026-10-30 without running its code, scripts/build_quadruple_stability.py)

stable_below.basis: classify_quad_2p2.py of the authors: a system is stable when the network's probability of 'unstable' is below 0.5

q_in_min.basis: paper section 3.1: masses log-uniform over one order of magnitude, so each inner mass ratio (m2/m1, m4/m3) is at least 0.1

q_out_max.basis: paper section 2 and the help text of classify_quad_2p2.py: q_out = (m3+m4)/(m1+m2) <= 1, the first binary being the heavier

eccentricity_max.basis: paper section 3.1: eccentricities uniform from 0 to 0.95

outer_orbits.basis: paper section 2: 'stable' means bound and not chaotic over 100 outer orbits (a ghost run with the inner axis of the lighter inner binary larger by 1e-6 au diverging by less than 1e-2 in that axis), not stable for a stellar lifetime

divergence_limit.basis: paper section 2: delta(t) = (a_orig - a_ghost) / a_orig above 1e-2 at any step is unstable

axis_margin.basis: GEN.1016: a system the 2+2 network calls stable is accepted only if it is still stable with both alpha_in1_out and alpha_in2_out multiplied by this number. Carried over from the 3+1 margin (quadruple_stability_3p1.json axis_margin, hand-tuned on 331 REBOUND 3+1 systems) with no 2+2 N-body sample behind it; an own 2+2 sample replaces it
